titleZh: 客人连住三晚，酒店每天该做什么不一样？
titleEn: A Guest Is Staying Three Nights. What Should the Hotel Do Differently Each Day?
summaryZh: 连住服务不是把一晚标准复制三次。酒店应按抵店前、第一天、第二天、第三天和离店前分别设计任务，并让前厅、客房、餐饮和销售完成交接。
summaryEn: Multi-night service is not a one-night template repeated three times. Hotels should design distinct tasks before arrival, on each day and before departure, supported by clear cross-department handoffs.
contentZh:
客人连住三晚，酒店每天该做什么不一样？

可以设想一个综合经营场景：一位客人在酒店住了四天，退房时说‘挺好的，就是每天都一样’。SOP全部执行到位，客人没有指出某一项明确故障，却也没有感受到服务随着停留时间发生变化。

这个场景揭示了一类容易被忽视的问题：如果酒店只把一晚的服务标准复制三天，即使没有明显投诉，也可能让客人觉得酒店缺少变化。真正的问题不是酒店没有标准，而是没有为多晚停留设计每天不同的任务。

第零天：抵店之前

连住服务的起点在客人预订之后。酒店可以确认同行人、预计抵店时间、出行目的，以及清扫或饮食偏好。带孩子的家庭和出差客需要不同的服务节奏。简单的抵店前消息就能帮助酒店提前准备婴儿床、加床或楼层需求。

第一天：建立安心感

第一天的核心不是惊艳，而是放心。酒店需要说清设施使用、Wi-Fi、紧急求助、早餐、周边便利设施和主要交通方式。信息不宜全部塞给客人，而应根据出行目的选择最相关的内容。

第二天：主动调整

经过第一晚，酒店可以结合客人主动表达的需求和已获授权记录，调整清扫时间、用品补给、早餐提示和周边建议。关键不是提供更多服务，而是根据已知信息调整，让客人感到被注意。

第三天及以后：制造变化

第三天需要低成本但可感知的变化。早餐可以按酒店规模和厨房条件轮换部分品类；公共空间可以提供时段建议；经过筛选的本地商户、步道或文化体验可以附上清晰说明和预约方式。所有推荐都应符合实际交付能力。

离店前一天：顺畅收尾

酒店可以提前确认账单、车辆、行李、发票、延住和延迟退房需求。把这些事情集中到最后一小时，会同时增加前台压力和客人等待。

四个部门怎样分工

前厅负责抵店前确认、第一天信息引导、后续服务提示和离店前确认。客房负责记录客人主动表达的清扫偏好和补给需求。餐饮负责可执行的早餐变化。销售和市场负责维护经过核验的本地合作信息。

信息交接不需要复杂系统。酒店可以按团队规模和班次，在晨会或共享记录中同步房号、入住天数、已确认偏好和下一步动作，并明确谁负责闭环。

常见问题

连住客房需要每天打扫吗？

不一定需要全套打扫，但应让客人选择。酒店可以询问清扫时间、频率、补充用品和毛巾更换需求，不应假设所有客人都接受同一套安排。

酒店怎样询问清扫偏好？

可以通过前台消息、房间电话或简短选择卡询问。重点是说明可选项目并获得客人同意，不根据未经授权的行为记录推断私人偏好。

连住客适合推荐哪些增值服务？

可以推荐洗衣、本地餐饮、半日路线、延迟退房或房型升级，但前提是与停留目的相关、价格透明且酒店能够稳定交付。

前厅和客房怎样交接连住客需求？

使用一张共享记录，列明房号、入住天数、客人主动确认的偏好、下一步动作和责任岗位。频率和形式按酒店规模与班次调整。

连住服务不是增加复杂流程，而是让每一天有不同任务：第一天安心，第二天调整，第三天创造变化，离店前顺畅收尾。了解更多：marvelbros.com/zh/hotel-operation-improvement
contentEn:
A Guest Is Staying Three Nights. What Should the Hotel Do Differently Each Day?

Consider a composite operating scenario. A guest stays four nights and describes the stay as ‘fine—just the same every day.’ Every SOP was followed. The guest did not identify a single failure, but the service never evolved with the length of stay.

This illustrates a quiet risk: when a hotel repeats a one-night template across a multi-night stay, the absence of a complaint does not mean the experience felt distinctive. Each day needs a different operational purpose.

Day Zero: Before Arrival

After booking, the hotel can confirm who is traveling, expected arrival time, trip purpose, and any cleaning or dietary preferences. A family and a business traveler need different service rhythms. A short pre-arrival message can also surface needs such as a crib, extra bed or floor preference.

Day One: Build Confidence

Day one should reduce uncertainty. Explain essential facilities, Wi-Fi, emergency help, breakfast, nearby conveniences and transport. Select the most relevant information for the guest's trip purpose instead of overwhelming every guest with the same list.

Day Two: Adjust Proactively

After the first night, use needs the guest has actively expressed and records the guest has authorized to adjust cleaning, supplies, breakfast guidance and local recommendations. The goal is not more service. It is a better response to known needs.

Day Three and Beyond: Create Variation

Introduce low-cost, perceptible variation. Rotate selected breakfast items according to kitchen capability, explain how public spaces change through the day, and recommend vetted local partners or routes with clear booking information. Every promise must match actual delivery capacity.

The Day Before Departure: Close Smoothly

Confirm billing, transport, luggage, invoice, extension and late-checkout needs in advance. Concentrating every decision in the final hour increases front-desk pressure and guest waiting.

How Four Departments Share the Work

The front desk handles pre-arrival confirmation, day-one orientation, later service prompts and pre-departure checks. Housekeeping records cleaning and supply preferences the guest has actively shared. F&B plans feasible breakfast variation. Sales and marketing maintain verified local-partner information.

The handoff does not require a complex system. Based on team size and shifts, hotels can use a brief meeting or shared record containing room number, length of stay, confirmed preferences, the next action and the accountable role.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do multi-night rooms need a full clean every day?

Not necessarily. Give guests a choice about cleaning time, frequency, supplies and towel replacement rather than assuming one schedule suits everyone.

How should hotels ask about cleaning preferences?

Use a front-desk message, room phone or short selection card. Explain the available choices and obtain consent instead of inferring private preferences from unauthorized behavior tracking.

What add-on services suit multi-night guests?

Laundry, local dining, half-day routes, late checkout or room upgrades may fit, provided they match the trip purpose, have transparent prices and can be delivered reliably.

How should front desk and housekeeping share multi-night needs?

Use one shared record listing room number, length of stay, preferences confirmed by the guest, the next action and the responsible role. Adapt the frequency and format to the hotel's scale and shifts.

Multi-night service does not require a complicated new system. It requires a different purpose for each day: confidence on day one, adjustment on day two, variation on day three and a smooth departure. Learn more: marvelbros.com/en/hotel-operation-improvement
author: MBCT（MarvelBros C&T）
